correctness.rationale: The 4 edge-orientation states of each length-two arm give 2z for the hub-outward edge and (1+z) for the hub-inward edge. Hub-sink correction yields (1+3z)^m+(z-1)(1+z)^m, with exact coefficients (3^k-1)C(m,k)+C(m,k-1). For negative z=-y, the parity and strict monotonicity of the two rational functions prove exactly one y>1 for every m and exactly one x in (1/2,1) for even m; the derivative at zero is 2m+1, and no positive root occurs. The limits y/3^m ->1 and x->1/2 follow from explicit logarithmic bounds. Executing artifacts/verify.py independently enumerated 21844 individual graph edge orientations (m=1..7), and exact signs/coefficients for m=1..40. Numerical results corroborate, do not substitute for, the all-order proof.

value.rationale: For a canonical infinite family of claw-containing chordal trees, the theorem gives both an all-coefficient enumerator and the exact real-root count and intervals at every order. It identifies a sharp real-rootedness cutoff (only path endpoints m=1,2), quantifies the growing nonreal-root population, and proves one negative root escapes at exponential scale 3^m while the even-parity root converges to -1/2. This addresses the boundary of recent claw-free real-rootedness theorems with structural information beyond routine evaluation or a finite table.
